worldtype_mapper.what: Maps a string to the WorldType enum: strncmp 'FTUE' (len 4) -> 0, 'OpenWorld' (len 9) -> 1, else 2 (Unknown). Confirms the wire token is the bare 'OpenWorld', not 'eWorldType_OpenWorld'.

worldmetadata_property_table.what: Registration table for the WorldMetadata property set. Each property is registered with a type-specific helper: FUN_144c6c330 (int, 2 args), FUN_144c60a10 (string/object), FUN_144c55a20 (enum), FUN_144c6c550, FUN_144c5b320, FUN_144c6a7f0 (bool). Real property names: worldId, name, type, status, version, publicStatusCode, publicName, maxAccountCharacters, worldSet, worldMetrics (nested WorldMetrics: worldAgeDays, queueSize, queueWaitTimeSec, worldPopulationStatus), transferToRegion, isFull, isRecommended. NOTE: name/type/status, NOT worldName/worldType/worldStatus.
worldmetadata_property_table.found_by: xrefs to the camelCase key block 0x1483c0900, all inside FUN_144f40780

worlds_info_accessor.what: Accessor for the WorldsInfo property (FNV-1a hash map lookup). Called from 0x144f55461 inside the big parser.

big_parser.what: 85 KB function containing the WorldMetadata/WorldMetrics property registration AND the only caller of the WorldsInfo accessor. This is the landing-screen world model: start here when hunting the world-list predicate.
big_parser.found_by: .pdata range containing all WorldMetadata property xrefs

state_record_bundle_parser.what: Walks a type-0x08 StateBundle body: [record_id VLQ][u8 fragment_count], then per-fragment FUN_146af2340 which reads [fragment_key VLQ] + [fragment_type_index VLQ] and dispatches the type object (vtable +0x90) to consume the payload. Record id 1 reaches the local-player branch in FUN_141717fc0.
state_record_bundle_parser.found_by: decompiled from the FUN_14643e7b0 -> FUN_146455e90 -> FUN_14175ccc0 call chain

local_player_metadata_branch.what: StateBundle record handler. Indexes state + 0x608 + record_id*0x10; record_id == 1 logs 'Received new local player metadata, updating m_localPlayersServerGDERef' and writes slot+0x850/+0x870/+0x880. In fresh PID 39284, the record-1 slot at state+0x618 changed from null to non-null across handler calls, while the separate possession-manager fields stayed null. This is the local-player/GDE metadata path; it does not itself establish possession.
local_player_metadata_branch.found_by: static call chain from the StateBundle parser

local_player_actor_prototype_builder.what: Builds a 0x210-byte temporary prototype through FUN_14161b9b0 and passes it to the only known direct caller of FUN_141563e20, the generic actor factory. It remains a candidate actor-construction path, not proven to be the missing local-player path. Read-only burst captures on PIDs 45592 and 54936 counted zero calls to FUN_141563e20, so this candidate was not reached in either replay burst. Game.log's category-3 local-player metadata trace is suppressed at the current level; its absence is not diagnostic.
local_player_actor_prototype_builder.found_by: Ghidra decompile of the actor-factory caller, build 1.400.6031.6004151

local_player_holder_getter.what: Manager context/local-player getter at vtable slot +0x30. Read-only captures on fresh PIDs 39284, 45592, and 39172 observed manager+0x08 and manager+0x10 as NULL after record-1 metadata produced non-null state-slot objects. Static vtable analysis identifies an indirect manager-context setter at slot +0x10 (FUN_146928d80); its caller gate was not satisfied during PID 39172's replay. The precise pointee type and StateBundle input that should activate the setter remain unresolved.
local_player_holder_getter.found_by: Ghidra vtable analysis + reverse/probes/client/frida-player-holder-snapshot.py after checking the exact private process had no EAC service/module

local_player_facet_uuid_field.what: The two string fields the possession gate reads on a player's facet entity, confirmed on the wire 2026-10-02: entity+0x7d0 = the player UUID (16 raw bytes formatted as a dashed GUID) and entity+0x880 = the display name. In every player's facet record the UUID is immediately followed by `[u8 len][name]`: other players show `45 29 88 c6 ... 45 e6 | 07 | "Unusual"`, the capture author's own record shows `<16 ZERO bytes> | 0a | "Mixed Nuts"` - i.e. the capture redacted the author's own UUID. The gate compares entity+0x7d0 with the character UUID in the client's local option store, so a zeroed span means the comparison can never succeed and the player is never possessed. Fix: world env AZOTH_REPLAY_LOCAL_PLAYER_UUID=character (javelin/replay_store.py::fill_local_player_uuid), which selects the redacted 16-byte span that is followed by a length-prefixed printable name. VERIFIED 2026-10-02 PID 25952/session 232: the world renders with the local player in it.
local_player_facet_uuid_field.found_by: wire analysis of the capture's redacted spans (services/world/replay/messages-redacted.txt) cross-checked with the live Frida samples of FUN_146929df0's two string arguments

local_player_context_manager_dispatch.what: Common state gate that can call the manager vtable slot +0x10. Manager vtable 0x148559dc0 resolves that slot to FUN_146928d80, which stores its second argument at manager+0x08, copies a shared reference from context+0x48/+0x50 into manager+0x10/+0x18, then calls slot +0x20. The dispatch calls the setter only when state+0x318 == 1, state+0x31c != 0, and state+0x31d == 0. Fresh PID 39172/REP session 1059 observed 39 dispatch entries, each with status 2, zero setter calls, zero local-player prototype-builder calls, and zero known actor-factory calls. These state objects are generic; their status-2 readings do not yet identify the missing local-player state. CORRECTED 2026-10-01 from Ghidra pseudocode: on status 1 the gate sets the one-shot latch state+0x31d = 1, then calls TWO setters - FUN_141025f70() vtable+0x20 with FUN_1416bc930(state)+0x20, and the manager FUN_141026080() vtable+0x10 (the context setter) with the context object FUN_1406c6a00(state) - then raises event UNK_1468918c0 via FUN_1466274a0(FUN_1416af450(state)). On status != 1 it skips both setters and only raises that event. So status is written by FUN_146929df0, and 1 means 'the wire option value equals the local option value' (see local_option_gate_status_writer).
local_player_context_manager_dispatch.found_by: Ghidra decompile of FUN_146764cd0 and the manager vtable, then read-only burst hooks in reverse/probes/client/frida-burst-capture.py; pseudocode re-read 2026-10-01 after the corpus completed

local_option_gate_status_writer.what: Sole writer of the gate status at state+0x318, called from FUN_14683c8d0 (PlayerComponentClientFacet vtable 0x148535728 slot +0xb0). Pseudocode: (1) looks up a local option value with FUN_140fca4e0(out_optional_string, &string_view{data=&UNK_1405717f0, size=0}); if the returned 'has value' byte is 0 it writes status 2. (2) Otherwise it compares that value with param_2 (a std::string) by size then memcmp, and writes status = (equal ? 1 : 2) - note that two EMPTY strings compare equal, so the docs' earlier 'both sides must be non-empty' wording is wrong; what is required is that the local store HAS an entry for the key. (3) It then calls the gate FUN_146764cd0(state) itself. (4) When status == 1 it also registers into a list at state+0x270/+0x288/+0x290 and dispatches through FUN_1416af4b0(*(state+8)) + FUN_14664c760(..., param_2, param_3). (5) When status != 1 it only logs via FUN_14664eab0(*(state+8)+0x58, ..., UNK_147f7f620). So: param_1 = the facet/state object whose +0x318 is the status, param_2 = entity+0x7d0 (the wire option string), param_3 = entity+0x880 (the value applied on success).
local_option_gate_status_writer.found_by: Ghidra pseudocode 2026-10-01 (corpus 8654f01d324636d9 complete) + capstone disasm of the same range

facet_option_apply_from_entity.what: PlayerComponentClientFacet vtable 0x148535728 slot +0xb0, reached once per facet. Reads the raw facet entity (param_2, the 0xb20-byte pool object) and forwards its fields to the client component FUN_1406c6a00(facet). The option branch is the decisive one: it probes *(entity+0x7c0)->vtable[0x60]() and, when that is empty, *(entity+0x870)->vtable[0x60](); if either reports a present value it calls FUN_146929df0(facet, entity+0x7d0, entity+0x880). Everything else in the function copies entity fields into component offsets (+0x4b8, +0x490, +0x4f0, +0x510..+0x520) and drives FUN_1465f2430 / FUN_1402bafb0. So the wire source of both strings is the fragment that fills the facet entity slots +0x7c0/+0x7d0 and +0x870/+0x880.

local_option_lookup.what: Looks up a local option value: gets the per-thread store with FUN_141027e40(), and if a provider exists at store+0x90 it calls FUN_140fdfd00(store+0x58, 0, 0, 0, out, key16) with a 16-byte key copy of its second argument; a hit returns non-zero with the found flag set. Otherwise it walks a list at store+0x20 (0x18-byte entries, guarded by an SRW lock at store+0x48) to build the string. Writing the k-th entry's value into the out std::optional<string>. The key used by FUN_146929df0 is the constant {data = &UNK_1405717f0, size = 0}.

local_option_store_thread_local.what: Getter of the option store that FUN_140fca4e0 reads. NOT a process-global: it is a thread-local holder (_DAT_14a2fb8a8, allocated through FUN_140fcfec0 with the TLS slot _DAT_14e85384), lazily created per thread, with a vtable at 0x147f20210, an SRW lock at +0x48, a provider list at +0x20 and a value map at +0x58. Do not model it as a global options document; anything that fills it is per-thread state.
local_option_store_thread_local.found_by: Ghidra pseudocode 2026-10-01 (corpus complete) + the TLS allocator call shape

It tests FUN_146165f20 on the entity key, then either builds/updates through FUN_141570190 or inserts into the portrayal table with FUN_1415e68b0. Its conditional call to FUN_14178ec80 is the removal path, not actor construction. Burst probe on PID 54936 observed 94 calls during the initial state replay.

replica_portrayal_remove.what: Removes/destroys portrayal state for an entity, including table and notification cleanup. It is not an actor create function; counting it as create was an earlier probe-label error.

javelin_stream_processor.what: Ctor of the 0x770-byte Javelin stream/codec processor (vtable 0x148590ab8, 35 slots, 2nd vptr 0x148590bb0 at +0x08). param_2 lands at +0x50 (the main-thread drain ring). +0x118 = the 0x168 outbound/codec object, +0x120/+0x128 = a refcounted ring-queue pair installed by FUN_146b6d600. Factory FUN_146b6c490.

game_connection_stream_processor_slot.what: Creates the stream processor (FUN_146b6c490) and stores it at connection+0x1000; wraps it in an 0x18 handle at +0x1048 (vtable 0x14844c9a8); starts via FUN_146466650(conn, 1|3). Also calls processor vtable +0x18 (FUN_146b6d600, the reset that installs the +0x120 ring) and slot +0x08 (FUN_146b70af0, installs the three connection listener cells at processor+0x58/+0x98/+0xd8). Log channel string 'GameConnection' at 0x1484fc8f0.
game_connection_stream_processor_slot.found_by: callers of 0x146b6c490 + windowed scan for disp 0x1000 in 0x146400000-0x146480000

javelin_iface_v6_inbound.what: 6-slot interface sub-vtable (V6) of the stream-processor family. Slot +0x10 = 0x146b71590 = 'mov rcx,[rcx+8]; jmp FUN_146b6eb70'. Handles are the 16-byte pair {sub_vtable, impl}; FUN_146b6d600 builds {0x1485915b8, proc} and hands it to FUN_146b6a270, so the transport calls slot +0x10 to push inbound bytes. Siblings: V4 0x148591558 -> FUN_146b6e190, V5 0x148591588 -> FUN_146b6e7c0.
javelin_iface_v6_inbound.found_by: ptrscan of .rdata for the thunks in 0x146b71280-0x146b71800 + disasm

javelin_inbound_decode_entry.what: Inbound packet entry (V6 slot +0x10). Accumulates the byte count at proc+0x710, builds a reader over the payload, inits a decode context with FUN_146154030, then deserializes with FUN_1461ac8d0; on failure it logs through FUN_146b6c500. On success it reaches javelin_inbound_type_dispatch at 0x146b6ed39. Reached only through the thunk 0x146b71594 (jmp), which is why a direct-call xref scan finds nothing.

javelin_inbound_type_dispatch.what: Compares the decoded object type against ten known GUID branches. Known hits are handled inline (several call FUN_146b6c500 for a diagnostic). Everything else - including fragment type 8A40 (GUID 8a40aec2-ae07-4f92-9bf3-78fc0cc94fdf, payload vtable 0x1484ff1d8) and index 972 (DE1A18A9-...) - takes the fallback at 0x146b6fde3 and pushes the exact {object, owner} pair into the ring at proc+0x120.
javelin_inbound_type_dispatch.found_by: decompile; branch GUIDs resolved via their getters

javelin_fallback_ring_queue.what: Getter for the proc+0x120 ring: returns {out[0]=proc+0x120, out[1]=proc+0x128} and bumps the strong refcount at [proc+0x128]+8. It is vtable slot 8 (+0x40) of the stream processor (stored at 0x148590af8) and has ZERO direct callers, so its only call sites are virtual 'call qword ptr [reg+0x40]'. Ring layout relative to proc+0x120: +0x00 owner thread id, +0x04 recursion, +0x08 SRW lock, +0x18 slot-pointer array, +0x20 capacity (power of two), +0x28 head, +0x30 count; each slot is a 16-byte {object, owner} pair.
javelin_fallback_ring_queue.found_by: ptrscan + .pdata lookup of the vtable slot

javelin_ring_queue_owner.what: Allocates the 0x48 refcounted ring-queue owner for proc+0x120/+0x128 (vtable 0x148591498, 42 slots = 12 own + 5 embedded 6-slot interface sub-vftables at 0x1485914f8/0x148591528/0x148591558/0x148591588/0x1485915b8). Layout: vptr+0x00, strong=1 at +0x08, weak=1 at +0x0C, queue at +0x10, SRW at +0x18, intrusive-list sentinel at +0x20. The pair stored at proc+0x120 is {owner+0x10, owner}. Dtor slot 0 = 0x146b713c0 (jmp FUN_146b6ac50(this+0x20)), scalar-deleting slot 2 = 0x146b6bd40 (frees 0x48).
javelin_ring_queue_owner.found_by: disasm of the alloc block in FUN_146b6d600 + vtable dump

javelin_fallback_ring_push.what: Pushes one {object, owner} pair into a ring queue. Same-thread fast path (gs:[0x48] == queue+0x00) bumps a recursion counter; otherwise AcquireSRWLockExclusive (IAT 0x147EC9350). Index = (capacity-1) & (count + head), head = (capacity-1) & head. Zeros the caller's pair and releases the owner refcount. Sole caller: the 0x146b6f190 fallback at 0x146b6fde3.
javelin_fallback_ring_push.found_by: disasm; single call site from callers_of

javelin_drain_ring_dispatch.what: THE inbound message dispatch. Pops {object, owner} LIFO from the ring at proc+0x50 (SRW lock, index = (capacity-1) & head), then per object: proc+0x48 = tick arg; call object->vtable[+0x30] (the type-GUID getter); FUN_140a174c0 turns the result into a 16-byte key; hash = FUN_14087cc20(key.lo ^ key.hi); bucket = proc+0x20[(hash & proc+0x38)] walked as 0x20-byte nodes with the key at +0x10/+0x18. On a hit it calls ((*(void**)node+0x20))[+0x08](node+0x28); on a miss it calls proc->vtable[+0x08]. Finally proc->vtable[+0x10] once per drain. Stops when proc+0x60 is set or the r8 budget is exhausted.
javelin_drain_ring_dispatch.found_by: field-set + SRW-IAT scan, then disasm; single caller is the frame tick

javelin_frame_tick_driver.what: Per-frame tick of the connection wrapper, which embeds the stream processor at +0xb0. Probes it with FUN_146b6d010 and, if live, calls FUN_146b6d180(processor+0xb0, tick_arg, 0) - i.e. this is the main-thread pump for the inbound object queue. Then FUN_145aa2f40 / FUN_145a99360 and the region/zone bookkeeping.

deferred_action_queue_drain.what: Called once per frame by FUN_141733f70; drains main/staging queues at object+0x1b8/+0x1d8 in 0x50-byte batches. The limit is cvar javelin.deferred-actions-max-depth at _DAT_14a321a4c; runtime default was 0, clamped to one batch. Fresh PIDs 39284 and 39172 emitted the recursion warning, but read-only sampling found both queues empty at every drain entry and no target lookups. A fresh-process value-16 experiment on PID 45476/session 1058 did not stop warnings or restore the black view. The warning alone does not identify a persistent queued action or explain the missing actor.

deferred_action_target_resolver.what: Resolves a queued action's target entity ID; queue entry target ID is at +0x48 and its vtable is at +0x00. Read-only probe on fresh PID 39284 observed no resolver calls while the frame was black.
deferred_action_target_resolver.found_by: xrefmap + decompile of deferred-action queue consumer

This is the factory the session-232 burst probe counted as 0. Lookup branch: FUN_14145b890. Caller: FUN_141763b88 chunk (entity from vtable+0x20), attach id 0x140, data 0x149e90cf8.

All called from FUN_141763950's continuation chunks with attach ids 0x120/0x140/0x180/0x1b8/0x201 (data 0x149e90c90/0x149e90cf8/0x149e90d00/0x149e90d08). All keyed by the same byte [+8] condition.

component_cluster_table_driven.what: Game-module reflected-component instantiation cluster (AZ behavior context). Each spawner creates a component by NAME (FNV-1a of the .rdata type-name string via FUN_141416740) when the container's byte [+8]==0, else resolves the existing one by 16-byte GUID via FUN_14145b890.

transform_guard_chain.what: MOVEMENT BLOCKER (closed 2026-10-02). FUN_141763b70(param_1) resolves the entity via param_1->vtable[+0x20](param_1, FUN_1407fbe80()) - FUN_1407fbe80 reads a TLS-indexed per-thread value (gs:[0x58]+slot*8 then +0x3684, same TLS pattern as the StateReplication trace level and the local-option store). replication_unreliable_gate_20261003.what: The client's replication gate, found 2026-10-03 by disassembling FUN_14643e7b0 (RVA 0x643E7B0, range 0x14643e7b0-0x14643f020, shard-001262.c:14587). This is the GameMessagePort handler that logs both 'HandleUnexpectedMessage skipping ReceiveStateBundle ... clientContext == nullptr' and 'MayHandleReplicationUnreliable() returning false ...'. GATE A (unreliable replication accepted or dropped), code 0x14643EAD1-0x14643EB15: al = FUN_1406c10a0(msg); r9d = byte [port+0x80] (m_clientContextInstanceId); if (al != r9b) goto reject; rdx = qword [port+0x78] (m_lastUnreliableReplicationSeq); rcx = *FUN_1406d97b0(msg) (the message's own seq); if (rdx == rcx) accept; if (rcx == -1) reject; if (rdx == -1) accept; if (rdx >= rcx) reject; else accept and store [port+0x78] = rcx. So an unreliable replication message is handled only when its clientContextInstanceId matches the port's AND its seq is STRICTLY GREATER than the high-water. Live 2026-10-03 22:50:54 UTC the client logged 'MayHandleReplicationUnreliable() returning false clientContextInstanceId 1 m_clientContextInstanceId 1 seq 39 m_lastUnreliableReplicationSeq 53' every ~2 s, i.e. the instance id matched and the seq was 14 below the high-water, so every one was dropped as already seen. Consequence for us: replaying captured bundles a second time cannot work by itself, because each captured message carries its original seq from the capture and the high-water is already past it. Any continuation must present a seq above the high-water. GATE B (ClientContext creation), code 0x14643EED2-0x14643EEFC: bl = FUN_146158ba0(...); if bl == 0 skip everything; al = FUN_1406c10a0(msg); if (al != [port+0x80]) goto 0x14643EF03 (the 'changing to' log path); else call FUN_146448cd0. Inside FUN_146448cd0 (range 0x146448cd0-0x14644918a) the Initialize step is 0x146448E40-0x146448E5F: rcx = [rdi+8]; call qword [*rcx + 0x18] = clientContext->Initialize; then log 'Calling clientContext->Initialize' (string 0x84FF598). It is guarded at 0x146448E20-0x146448E23 by rdi (the EOS ClientSDK object, global read at 0x146448E16) being non-null; when it is null the code logs 'entSdk is nullptr' instead. FUN_146448cd0's only caller is 0x14643EEE9 in FUN_14643e7b0. MEASURED SESSION BUG: in one client process (pid 38872) session 1 created the context ('Calling clientContext->Initialize' at 21:01:59 UTC, 1 skipped bundle) but sessions 2 and 3, after the same process disconnected and re-logged in at 21:54:04 and 22:13:59 UTC, never logged Initialize and produced 96+ skipped bundles each: with no ClientContext every state bundle is dropped, so the world never advances and no local body can exist. A fresh NewWorld.exe is therefore required after any disconnect; a server-side fix cannot repair that process in place. The HUD field behind 'Time since last response' is separate: FUN_14487b300 (shard-000990.c:8110) prints FUN_141413890() - *(obj+0xAA8), and FUN_14486c740 (shard-000991.c:14461, ~0x14486C852) does the same and sets state 2 once the gap exceeds the runtime global _DAT_149f21054 (RVA 0x9F21054, runtime-initialised so its file bytes are not the value). Neither function writes +0xAA8 and neither runs on a timer: a Frida hook on both saw zero calls while the client sat at character select, and MemoryAccessMonitor on +0xAA8 is armed the moment either fires. Also implemented and measured in services/world: the post-replay 0x08 state stream (AZOTH_REPLAY_STATE_STREAM, loops the captured tail seq 0xa0..0xb0 every 2 s). In a fresh session it kept OnLocalNetworkConnectionWarning at 0 for the first ~5 minutes, but the client rejects those bundles through GATE A, so it is not a fix yet. Movement was re-tested in that session and still fails (W held 1.5 s as scan code 0x11: changed>8 8.28%, motion ratio 0.12x). Found 2026-10-03.

STATIC: FUN_141582430 has exactly ONE E8 caller in the whole .text, 0x141763BD5, inside FUN_141763b70. FUN_14169a210 has ZERO E8 callers. client_self_reconnect_kills_context_2026.what: MEDIDO 2026-10-04, sesion viva (pid 68096), sobre el log del cliente y el del servidor. EL CLIENTE SE RECONECTA SOLO ~5 s DESPUES DEL SPAWN, en medio del replay. Timeline exacta de Game.log (UTC): 11:26:54.392 'player spawn succeeds' + estado InGame; 11:26:56.278 'LevelInfoChanged'; 11:26:56.279 'LevelInfoChanged m_clientContextInstanceId 0 changing to levelInfo.m_clientContextInstanceId 1'; 11:26:59.216 '[OmniAuthBackend] AGS account link session ended'; 11:26:59.224 'CGame::ActorContainerConnect' (el cliente ARRANCA una conexion nueva) y en el mismo milisegundo 'GameConnectionWrapper::Disconnect' + 'CGame::OnDisconnection: Disconnected from REP'. Del lado del servidor, en esa ventana el replay iba por el seq 15 de 137, sin ningun error: la caida no la provoca el servidor, la decide el cliente. En esa primera sesion NO hay ninguna linea 'Calling clientContext->Initialize' antes del corte. En la segunda sesion (spawn 11:27:17.783) SI aparece 'Calling clientContext->Initialize' a las 11:27:28.132, y a las 11:29:38 el cliente vuelve a caerse ('disconnected from REP' + mm_csdkerr). Tercera sesion: spawn 11:29:55.562, aviso del cable a las 11:29:57, y desde las 11:30:00 el log se llena de 'HandleUnexpectedMessage skipping ReceiveStateBundle ... clientContext == nullptr' (cientos de lineas). CONSECUENCIA (es la explicacion de todo lo demas): cada reconexion deja al cliente SIN ClientContext, y sin ClientContext descarta TODO el estado del mundo. Por eso el jugador local no tiene componentes de fisica, por eso WASD no mueve nada, y por eso el aviso del cable sube hasta que se cae otra vez. La sesion 'sana' es solo la primera: cuando se midio '1 solo bundle descartado y sin desconexion' era una primera sesion que todavia tenia el contexto. DATOS COMPLEMENTARIOS: (a) el contador de resends del servidor no es una inundacion: ~300-450 por minuto, 5-7 por segundo; lo notable es que ~4400 datagramas llegan al tope de 6 intentos y se descartan, o sea que el cliente NO los ackea. (b) Hay 2 eventos 'dtls-session-reset' porque el cliente reusa su puerto de origen. (c) El gateway SI sirve POST /auth/platform/user/code con {"code": "AZOTH-PRIVATE", "statusCode": 0} (app.py, ruta is_platform_user_code_path), pero el cliente registra '[OmniAuthBackend] AGS account link error: omni::session::GetAccountLinkActionCode returned code: 203'; 203 es error de PARSEO segun el docstring de routes/omni.py, asi que la forma de esa respuesta no es la que espera OmniSDK. No probado que ese error sea la causa del corte (el corte del 11:26:59 es 2,5 min posterior a ese error), pero es una respuesta nuestra con forma equivocada. (d) Con el foco forzado, mantener W produce EXACTAMENTE UNA forma nueva en el trafico saliente: (canal 0, flags 0x19, 36 bytes) con cuerpo 81011705fc0c2000020316fdffff200621002400012f012f...; es un acuse, NO un delta de movimiento. En reposo esa forma no aparece nunca. Found 2026-10-04.

capture_redactions_block_player_state_20.what: Diagnostico de bloqueo del ClientContext, 2026-10-04. CADENA COMPLETA: (1) el cliente entra al mundo (player spawn succeeds); (2) LevelInfoChanged llega y fija port[+0x80] = 1; (3) el cliente espera el SIGUIENTE mensaje cuya identidad coincida con la puerta FUN_146158ba0 (VA 0x146158ba0: cmp rcx,rdx / je igual / [rcx+0x18]==[rdx+0x18] / [rcx+0x20]==[rdx+0x20] -> 1) para llamar a FUN_146448cd0 -> clientContext->Initialize; (4) no llega y a los ~3 s el cliente decide reconectar por si mismo (ActorContainerConnect + Disconnect); (5) en la reconexion el ClientContext NUNCA se vuelve a crear, asi que el cliente descarta TODO el estado del mundo (cientos de 'skipping ReceiveStateBundle ... clientContext == nullptr'); (6) sin ese estado el jugador local no tiene componentes de fisica, por eso WASD no mueve nada y el cable sube. POR QUE NO LLEGA: el mensaje que el cliente espera es el state bundle 0x08, y en el capture son los 5 mas grandes (seq 0x25/0x2a/0x2b/0x2e/0x2f, 46407-46423 bytes cada uno). CADA UNO tiene 453 redacciones de 36 bytes (el UUID del jugador/cuenta original, puesto a XX), mas 9420 bytes totales de huecos por mensaje. Con esos huecos el cliente no puede reconstruir los componentes del jugador (incluido el rigid body/character controller), y sin ellos la identidad que la puerta compara no coincide. El replay rellena solo las 6 ranuras explicitas del allowlist REPLAY_IDENTITY_TARGETS (REPLAY_IDENTITY_REMAP) y AZOTH_REPLAY_LOCAL_PLAYER_UUID (character), que cubren 36 bytes en seqs 0x28/0x73/0x98/0x9A/0x9C/0x9E; los otros 24.792 bytes de huecos quedan en cero. EL COMPARADOR: FUN_146158ba0 (VA 0x146158ba0) es un operator== de tres lineas: cmp rcx,rdx / [rcx+0x18]==[rdx+0x18] / [rcx+0x20]==[rdx+0x20]. Un fallo ahi significa que la identidad del mensaje y la del puerto difieren. POR QUE EL CAPTURE NO ALCANZA: el capture es de build 1.365, el cliente es 1.400.6031. Los bundles de 46 KB contienen el estado completo del mundo del capture, no el nuestro; incluso sin redacciones, el estado seria el del personaje del capture, no el del jugador de Azoth. CONCLUSION DE ARQUITECTURA: el cliente no se puede estabilizar retransmitiendo el capture. El servidor tiene que implementar el protocolo de replicacion real: crear la entidad del jugador con sus componentes (incluido el rigid body/character controller), mandarle el estado con las identidades correctas, y responder al input. Eso es lo que hace el servidor real para miles de jugadores sincronizados. Found 2026-10-04.

eos_anticheat_transport_gap_20261004.what: CAUSA RAIZ DE LA DESCONEXION A LOS ~52 s, medida 2026-10-04. Patron constante en TODAS las sesiones (7 partidas en dos dias): el cliente hace 'player spawn succeeds', el ClientContext se crea (en la primera sesion), y entre 5 y 52 segundos despues el ClientSDK reporta 'Unexpected client disconnect! {transportError: 4}' + '@mm_csdkerr_disconnect (4)' + 'JavelinGame::OnConnectionFail' y la conexion REP se cierra. El patron es identico en 1.365 y 1.400, con y sin el stream 0x08, con y sin el patch del watchdog. El stub EOS corre (su log dice 'ready' y sigue vivo), el patch del watchdog esta aplicado, y el servidor NO cierra la DTLS. La causa es el canal anticheat: el EOS ClientSDK espera que el servidor le mande mensajes anticheat por el REP; cuando no llegan en el tiempo esperado, reporta transportError 4 y el juego corta la conexion completa. El stub EOS solo enmascara las llamadas del resolver (FUN_1444f79e0 -> 0x444f79e0): devuelve EOS_Success en BeginSession/EndSession/Tick/Initialize, un fake handle en Get*Interface/Create, y 1 en AddNotify* — pero NO implementa el canal de datos anticheat (ReceiveMessageFromServer devuelve 0 = no hay datos). CONSECUENCIA EN CADENA: la conexion se corta -> el cliente se reconecta -> el ClientContext no se recrea (la puerta FUN_14643e7b0 -> FUN_146448cd0 exige que el clientContextInstanceId del mensaje coincida con port[+0x80]) -> el cliente descarta TODO el estado del mundo (cientos de 'skipping ReceiveStateBundle ... clientContext == nullptr') -> el jugador local queda sin componentes de fisica -> WASD no mueve nada -> el cable sube. PARA ARREGLARLO: hay dos caminos. (A) Implementar el canal anticheat en el servidor: interceptar los mensajes que el cliente manda al EOS anticheat server (los que llegan como typed-stream desconocidos) y responder con lo que el ClientSDK espera, para que el transport no reporte error 4. (B) Hookear el ClientSDK en el cliente para que ReceiveMessageFromServer devuelva un payload valido que el juego no interprete como error, o para que OnConnectionFail no corte la conexion REP. (B) es mas corto pero requiere RE del formato que el juego espera. (A) es lo correcto para la vision de miles de jugadores. Found 2026-10-04.

activity_stream_1b88_cable_ab_20261004.what:
A/B of a post-replay 0x1b88 activity stream (AZOTH_REPLAY_ACTIVITY_STREAM=1, world restarted with it on 19:45 UTC). HYPOTHESIS (from ingame_activity_timer): the InGame activity clock FUN_146445e10 reads processor+0x608 and the dispatcher FUN_146b6f190 refreshes it on its MISS path (message GUID not one of the ten singletons); our post-replay stream (0x15d ping + ch3 keepalive) never takes that path, so the red-cable warning appears within seconds of spawn. The capture's only verbatim repeatable body is the 42-byte type-0x1b88 message (23 byte-identical copies, seqs 0x0c..0x24, no redaction); served every 0.5 s with a fresh envelope seq after the replay drains, body verbatim. BASELINE, same evening 19:25 UTC (session 1, stream off): spawn 19:25:29.456, clientContext->Initialize 19:25:28.335 (3.1 s BEFORE spawn), ch0 burst ends 14 s after spawn (last replay envelope seq 1318 at 19:25:38), transportError 4 + @mm_csdkerr_disconnect (4) + JavelinGame::OnConnectionFail at 19:25:48.443 = 19.0 s after spawn. Session 2 (self-reconnect, 19:26:30): zero ClientContext from spawn (80 'skipping ReceiveStateBundle ... clientContext == nullptr'), warning climbed 1->12 in ~6.5 min (19:26:46 -> 19:32:09), no disconnect (the watchdog patch holds OnConnectionFail off). EXPERIMENT (session 3, spawn 19:51:23.674, entered from character select via WM_KEYDOWN VK 0x0D through scripts/post-input.py): clientContext->Initialize 19:51:27.606 (+3.9 s), ONE skipped bundle at 19:51:27.625 (load-order, same as baseline), then 11+ minutes InGame with ZERO further skipped bundles, ONE OnLocalNetworkConnectionWarning total (19:53:28.397, countReceived 1, +2m05s after spawn) and NO further warnings through 20:02:50 (1271 activity-stream messages, envelope seqs ~1350..3262), NO transportError 4, NO Connection fail, NO self-reconnect. LONG-RUN CORRECTION (checked 20:41 UTC): the session is still alive at 50+ min with ZERO transportError 4, but the warning counter RESUMES: a burst of OnLocalNetworkConnectionWarning starts at 20:17:23 UTC (231 lines by 20:31). The quiet window 19:53:28 -> 20:17:23 (24 min, one warning) is a 10x improvement over the baseline (12 warnings in 6.5 min), but the 0x1b88 stream does NOT permanently silence the clock. Confound: a read-only Frida probe attached at 20:11 UTC (frida-eos-stub, counters only) and the burst starts 6 min later; the earlier attach A/B (gametransform_attach_ab) showed native-call stalls correlate with the warning path, so the probe is a suspect correlate, not proof the stream decays. Next A/B must separate them: same stream, no Frida attach, watch the warning timeline. FINAL OUTCOME (20:31:23 UTC, session closed): the disconnect arrived as a plain 'CGame::ActorContainerDisconnect -> disconnected from REP' with NO transportError 4 anywhere in the session - the first measured disconnect without code 4 - after warning 231. Session lifetime: spawn 19:51:23 -> disconnect 20:31:23 = EXACTLY 40.0 min InGame with one ClientContext (baseline: 19.0 s). The 0x1b88 stream pushed the kill from 19 s to 40 min and changed the failure signature; the warning burst (post-probe-attach) preceded the kill by 14 min and is the remaining work item: either the stream's refresh decays after ~25 min or the Frida probe stall accelerated it. HISTORICAL INTERPRETATION, SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11: this run suggested the connection-kill and warning climb were separate symptoms and that 0x1b88 reduced the warning count. It lasted 40 minutes before disconnecting; this did not prove a stable user-visible connection, a causal clock refresh, or an ALC handshake. The 19 s transportError-4 of the baseline happened WITH the stream off, so code 4 is NOT a fixed anticheat-channel timeout - it is the InGame timeout path (error 0x35 per ingame_activity_timer) after the clock goes stale, and the clock is refreshed by a miss-path message. CAUSALITY OF THE STAMP PATH STILL UNPROVEN: 0x1b88's GUID may be a miss-path GUID by luck; a next session could A/B the period (0.5 s vs 2 s) to find the actual refresh budget. MOVEMENT IS STILL THE OPEN BUG and it is server-independent: the local entity has a transform but no physics components; follow FUN_141763b70 (gametransform attach gate), NOT the connection.

movement_replication_asymmetry_20261005.what: MEASURED 2026-10-05 (desktop session, fresh pid 26908, world loaded 19:03:25Z). javelin_prefix_varint.what: The shared varint every typed message and every state-bundle field uses. ENCODING: the number of LEADING 1-BITS in the first byte gives the number of continuation bytes n (0..4); the first byte's remaining low 7-n bits are the LOWEST bits of the value and the continuation bytes are a LITTLE-ENDIAN integer placed above them: value = (LE(cont) << (7-n)) | (b0 & ((1 << (7-n)) - 1)). Widths: 1 byte below 0x80, then 2/3/4/5 bytes with capacities 2^14/2^21/2^28/2^35. Verified against capture bytes: type 0x15d = 9d 05, 0x1b88 = 88 6e, 0x663 = a3 19, 0x16a0 = a0 5a, and the spawn fragment length 46393 = d9 a9 05. Decoding every server->client message type in the capture round-trips 137 of 138 (the exception is seq 0x25, the datagram-first case). TRAP: Ghidra renders the 3-byte branch as a big-endian CONCAT21 shifted by 4; big-endian makes d9 a9 05 equal 1384633, which is LARGER than the 46407-byte message containing it, so the big-endian reading is falsified by the data. Trust the bytes. Implementation with tests: services/world/src/azoth_world/javelin/varint.py.
javelin_prefix_varint.found_by: decompile of FUN_14087b5c0 + validation against all 138 server->client capture messages, 2026-10-09

Parsed against all 79 server->client 0x08 bodies in services/world/replay/messages-redacted.txt: 78 consume their body EXACTLY to the last byte; the only exception is seq 0x25, the first message of its datagram, which carries a datagram-level preamble. record_id 1 is the local-player metadata slot (it logs 'Received new local player metadata'), and the captured record ids span 1..0x35. The record header reader is FUN_146af20d0, the per-fragment reader is FUN_146af2340 (key varint, then type via FUN_1461ad130 -> FUN_1461acfe0, then the payload through the type object's vtable +0x90). This supersedes the earlier one-line note that gave the same shape without the kind byte, the 3-byte fragment prefix or the length field, and it is the first description that actually consumes a body exactly. Implementation with tests: services/world/src/azoth_world/javelin/bundle.py.

aoi_trait_system.what: The server-side replication architecture behind every entity and component the client sees. It is an AREA-OF-INTEREST TRAIT system, namespace Amazon::Hub::Aoi, with 185 traits in this build (PhysicsTrait, SpawnerTrait, PlayerManagerTrait, RoutingTrait, GridTrait, PersistenceSpawnerTrait, ...). Each trait replicates state to clients as RECORDS carrying FRAGMENTS, which is exactly what the type-0x08 state bundle transports, and the Javelin-level counterparts are UpdateRecordsMsg / FragmentUpdateMsg / RequestRecordsMsg / ResetRecordMsg / StartObservingFragmentMsg (see the registry's record_fragment family). PHYSICS IS ONE OF THESE TRAITS: PhysicsTrait owns a State type with GUID {F05E34C6-AF1E-476D-9472-5FC118FC4503} (found as the 'PhysicsTrait::State' descriptor next to the 'javelin-server.detection-volume-max-tracked-agents' CVar) and registers a message family RegisterRigidBodyMsg / UnregisterRigidBodyMsg / UpdateRigidBodyMsg / UpdateRigidBodyFilterMsg / UpdateRigidBodyRaidIdMsg / RegisterRigidBodyByAssetMsg, visible as the mangled template names Amazon::Hub::Aoi::PhysicsTrait::RegisterRigidBodyMsg. CONSEQUENCE for the private server: rigid bodies reach the client through this record/fragment path, NOT through the by-name component creator (FUN_141416740, measured never to run during world entry) and NOT through the replay, whose 79 captured fragments all carry type_index 1. Giving the local player physics therefore means implementing record/fragment replication for PhysicsTrait, which is the same machinery NPCs need.
aoi_trait_system.found_by: string scan for trait names + descriptor region read + mangled-name namespaces, 2026-10-09

az_type_table_index_is_wire_type.what: private-client/runtime/typeindex.json is the AZ type registry for this build (7052 GUIDs) and its POSITION is the wire type number, so index -> GUID -> message name is the whole addressing scheme. The Javelin message table (javelin-messages.json) is therefore a sparse subset of this registry: 142 of its 144 entries appear in it, and each entry's wire_type is its index here. The table also carries non-message types: PhysicsTrait::State = F05E34C6AF1E476D94725FC118FC4503 at index 933 (0x3a5), and fragment type 972 (0x3cc) = DE1A18A9CE9E43368DF8698A73C579D4. NOTE the physics COMPONENT guids (CharacterPhysicsComponent D707D6C5-3EFA-4275-82EB-A954F845D324, CharacterControllerComponent E9D84B77-422A-4DCB-9EFF-708120B1B1A0, GameRigidBodyComponent 5BA2D1FC-DB9D-4B81-88C9-89787D5C19F1, Transform 484AE67D-ABD0-4D9C-B2C8-9BB0EEC900E0) are ALL ABSENT from this table, so a component cannot be addressed by type index; only types the registry knows can. That is consistent with physics replicating through the PhysicsTrait record path rather than as a bare component.

movement_interaction_system_20261009.what: Movement in this build is expressed as a MOVEMENT INTERACTION with its own id and state machine, not as a bare position update. Strings in the image name the pieces: 'AbortMovement, default actor to removed: actorId=', 'for active movement interaction: actorId=', 'from PendingMove to Active due to cancel. movementInteractionId=', 'from PendingMove to Active due to timeout. movementInteractionId=', 'with no active movement interaction. The actor was already ...', 'movement, need to wait for it', 'AllowMovementAfterReachingTargetPos', and a paired 'Client: m_movement = '%d'' / 'Server: m_movement = '%d''. So an actor is moved by starting an interaction (PendingMove), having it become Active, and it can be cancelled, time out, or abort. This matches the named family the message registry carries: StartMovementCommunicationMsg, CheckMovementStatusMsg, AckMovementMsg, CommitMovementMsg, AbortMovementMsg, CancelMovementMsg, MovementTimeoutMsg, ProcessDeferredMovementRequestsMsg. SEPARATELY, movement input is gated by an input-filter system: PlayerInputFiltersComponent + PlayerInputFiltersComponentClientFacet + PlayerInputFiltersRequestBus expose EnableInputFilter / EnableInputFilterWithContext / IsInputFilterEnabled / CreateInputFilter / AddActionMapActionsToInputFilter / InputFilterToggle. This is a second, independent candidate for why WASD does nothing: a disabled input filter would swallow the action before it reaches movement, and it would look exactly like the measured behaviour (keys reach the UI, the camera rotates, WASD produces no movement and no outbound delta). Not yet measured which of the two is the operative blocker.
movement_interaction_system_20261009.found_by: image string scan for movement/input-filter vocabulary, 2026-10-09

activity_clock_starvation_20261010.what: THE 27-SECOND DISCONNECT, measured live 2026-10-10 with the recommended gate block. Timeline: 00:29:47.751Z 'player spawn succeeds, in game'; 00:30:14.570Z 'disconnected from REP' + 'Unexpected client disconnect! {transportError:4}'; 00:30:14.587Z 'Update state InGame to new state Disconnected'. So the transport dropped 26.8 s after the spawn, and the automatic retry that followed never re-created the ClientContext, so every later bundle was skipped with 'clientContext == nullptr'. ROOT CAUSE: the two emitters that keep the client's InGame activity clock alive (the 0x15d heartbeat and the 0x1096/0x1097 input response) both gated on `self.replay_queue` being EMPTY. The captured replay is 82 messages but ~1090 Carrier chunks (24 of the captured bodies are 46 KB), and at the recommended AZOTH_CHUNK_GAP_MS=20 that needs ~22 s -- inside the client's ~27 s watchdog. In that run the server log contained ZERO `heartbeat` and ZERO `input-response` events for the whole session, while the client's OnLocalNetworkConnectionWarning climbed to 22. FIX: those two emitters now gate on `_post_replay_started()` (the post-V3 greetings only) and run CONCURRENTLY with the replay, which is what the capture shows the real server doing. The state stream deliberately keeps the drained-replay requirement: it re-applies the same captured bundles, and double-applying state is not idempotent client-side. RESULT of the re-run with the fix: transportError 0, 'disconnected from REP' 0, OnLocalNetworkConnectionWarning 1, session alive past 128 s, and the world renders with the player, NPCs and the full HUD (screenshot in research/sessions/2026-10-10/). Separately, the same session exposed a second bug: the server's 16-bit envelope sequence was unmasked, so the keepalive raised `OverflowError: int too big to convert` once next_out_seq passed 65535 and stayed dead for two hours (7395 tick errors); see PRIVATE-CLIENT-RUNBOOK.md gate 8e.

inject_lever_validation_20261010.what: The `inject` lever (`services/world/inject.hex` + `PeerSession.maybe_inject`, driven by `scripts/world-inject.py`) was exercised against a LIVE session on 2026-10-10 and it settles three things. So the layout in bundle.py is correct as far as the client is concerned, not merely self-consistent. (2) A `StartMovementCommunicationMsg` (wire type 0x2d6, marker `00 01 96 0b`) with an EMPTY body was also accepted silently: no decode warning, no ValidationError. statebundle_call_chain_verified_20261010.what: The state-bundle call chain, verified by call-graph rather than by adjacency: FUN_14643e7b0 (the GameMessagePort handler that logs 'skipping ReceiveStateBundle ... clientContext == nullptr') -> FUN_146455e90 -> FUN_14175ccc0 -> FUN_146af20d0 -> FUN_146af2340. Each edge is a real call in the decompiled body, so the bundle parser is no longer identified by positional guesswork. The call site in FUN_14175ccc0 is the most informative: `lVar14 = FUN_146af20d0(&reader, &out_record_id, &fragment_vector)` then `FUN_141717fc0(state, out_record_id, &fragment_vector, *FUN_1406d97b0(msg), byte[msg+8], lVar14, FUN_1406c10a0(msg))`. So FUN_146af20d0 fills a u16 RECORD ID and a VECTOR OF FRAGMENT OBJECTS, and FUN_141717fc0 receives both plus the message's seq and instance id. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the fragments in that vector are OBJECTS, not raw payloads -- FUN_146af2340 creates one per fragment (the vtable+0x90 call consumes the payload and the result is stored as a smart pointer). And FUN_141717fc0 indexes a handler table at `state + 0x608 + record_id*0x10`, so the record id is a HANDLER INDEX, which is why record_id 1 is the local-player metadata slot that logs 'Received new local player metadata'.

movement_absent_from_the_wire_20261010.what: MOVEMENT IS NOT SENT, measured live 2026-10-10 with the player in world. Two measurements. (1) Holding W for 2 s produces NO movement-family message in either direction. Decoding every client->server record in that window gives zero StartMovementCommunicationMsg (0x2d6), zero AckMovementMsg, zero CommitMovementMsg, zero MoveActorMsg, zero ReceivePlayerPositionClientMsg -- and zero type-0x635 records either, because the local-player state stream is not a typed message. replication_architecture_20261010.what: The complete replication architecture, now mapped end to end. There are THREE distinct message systems and confusing them is what made the protocol look opaque. (1) AOI TRAITS (82 traits, 2276 trait/message pairs, research/atlas/aoi-trait-registry.json): server-side authority for entity and component state. A trait replicates state as RECORDS carrying FRAGMENTS, which is exactly what the type-0x08 StateBundle transports. The record id selects a handler at `state + 0x608 + record_id*0x10`. (2) CLIENT MESSAGES (1783 RMIs, Hub::Javelin::ClientMessages): component-facet method calls named '<Component><Client|Server>Facet_<Method>', dispatched by facet target id -- this is the system behind the live warning 'RMIDispatch: The facet target ID couldn't be found ... GlobalStorageComponentClientFacet_ReceiveStorageSearchItems', i.e. the server calls a facet method on a facet the client does not have. (3) JAVELIN TYPED MESSAGES (144, research/atlas/javelin-messages.json): session/hub/movement control, carrying a wire type number. THE SPAWN/POSSESSION PROTOCOL is in system (1) and is now readable: the client asks with PlayerSpawnPointRequestTrait::RequestPlayerSpawnPointMsg, the server answers with PlayerSpawnPointResponseTrait::ReceivePlayerSpawnPointSuccessMsg (or ...FailureMsg), the manager then runs PlayerManagerTrait::ProcessSpawnQueueMsg, and the actual body is created through PrefabSpawnRequestTrait::RequestSpawnPrefabMsg (or PlayerManagerDebugTrait::DebugSpawnSliceMsg for a slice). PlayerManagerTrait also owns DeregisterCharacterMsg, RequestLocationRespawnActivePlayerMsg, RequestShutdownCharacterMsg and RequestReconnectCrossWorldMsg. PHYSICS is registered separately: PhysicsTrait::RegisterCharacterMsg / RegisterCharacterWithRepulsorsMsg (see aoi_trait_registry_20261010). So 'give the player a body' is not one message: it is a spawn-point handshake, a spawn-queue process, a prefab spawn, AND a physics registration, and the capture only contains the first part.
replication_architecture_20261010.found_by: mangled trait-hook scan + ClientMessages prefix analysis, 2026-10-10

fragment_model_needs_revision_20261010.what: LIVE MEASUREMENT that CORRECTS the container model. Hooked FUN_146af2340 (the per-fragment reader, in the verified call chain) on a running session and read the decode context cursor at [ctx+0x10] before and after each call; the delta is the bytes the client actually consumed for that fragment. Results: 720 calls in one session, with consumed sizes of 6, 9, 10, 13 (x4), 14, 15 (x2), 17, 21 (x2), 23, 28, 29 (x2), 40 (x2), 47, 69, 91, 109, 146, 532, 653, 1382, 4754, 5913, 17176 bytes -- i.e. HIGHLY variable, and many of them SMALL. Our capture parse concluded each type-0x08 body holds ONE record with ONE fragment carrying a huge payload (46393 bytes for the spawn, ~700-1000 for the tail bundles). Both cannot be true. The likely resolution is visible in FUN_14175ccc0: its body LOOPS, calling FUN_146af20d0 repeatedly (`lVar14 = FUN_146af20d0(...)`, then `lVar24 = lVar24 + 1`, then another FUN_146af20d0 when the reader is not exhausted). So a bundle body is probably a SEQUENCE of records, each `[varint record_id][u8 fragment_count][fragments...]`, repeated until the body ends -- and our parser read the FIRST record and then swallowed every following record as the first fragment's payload. METHODOLOGICAL LESSON: 'the parse consumes the body exactly' is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT evidence for a container layout; a model that treats the remainder as an opaque payload always consumes exactly. The distinguishing test is the client's own consumption, which is what this probe measures. Note this does NOT invalidate the varint (independently validated against 137 capture message types) nor the typed marker; it invalidates the record/fragment COUNT and therefore the fragment header layout.
fragment_model_needs_revision_20261010.found_by: live Frida cursor-delta probe on FUN_146af2340, 2026-10-10

statebundle_record_model_VERIFIED_202610.what: VERIFIED MODEL of the type-0x08 StateBundle body, from the client's own reads. Supersedes the earlier 'one record, one fragment' reading. LAYOUT: `[00 01 varint(0x08)]` marker, then an 8-byte prologue `01 <varint V> 01 01 01 01 00 00` (offsets 3-10; the first six of those are INVARIANT across all 78 captured bundles, and V varies), then a VARINT PAYLOAD LENGTH, then the payload. THE PAYLOAD IS A SEQUENCE OF RECORDS, each `[u8 record_id][u8 fragment_count][fragment x fragment_count]`. EVIDENCE 1 (the decisive one): a live Frida probe on FUN_146af20d0 measured, for each record, the bytes it consumed and the number of nested FUN_146af2340 calls (= fragments). The fragment count byte EQUALS the measured nested-call count in every one of 90 distinct records: `01 30`->48, `01 09`->9, `02 03`->3, `03 01`->1, `0d 06`->6, `1d 13`->19. EVIDENCE 2: byte-exact on the 78-byte bundle (seq 0xab). Its payload length is 66 and the payload is TWO records of exactly 33 bytes each, `48 03 03 0c 01 01 08 04 b2 2d 01 01 00 00 0a 01 02 53 ed 72 2b 64 01 46 c5 03 65 f2 69 14 78 61 58` and the same with `49 03`; 33+33=66 exactly, and the client measured consumed=33/frags=3 for each. EVIDENCE 3: record_ids are SEQUENTIAL across the session (1,2,3,...,0x2e, then 0x48,0x49,0x4a), which is what a handler index looks like -- and FUN_141717fc0 indexes exactly that at `state + 0x608 + record_id*0x10`. So record_id is the handler selector. WHY THE OLD PARSE LOOKED RIGHT: it read the prologue's bytes as `[kind][record_id][fragment_count]` and then treated the entire length-prefixed payload as ONE fragment's payload. That consumes the body exactly, which is why it passed -- but 'consumes exactly' cannot discriminate when the remainder is opaque. The real fragment_count for the spawn record is 48, not 1. STILL OPEN: the 8-byte prologue's V field (varies, 53 distinct values across the capture, unrelated to the record count) and the FRAGMENT layout inside a record (a fragment is not `[key][type][3 bytes][length][payload]` as previously assumed; the spawn's 48 fragments measured 23, 146, 109, 40, 5913, 14, 28, 10, 4754, 47, 15, 532, 17, 13, 15, 69, 91, 21, 6, 653, 13, 17176, 40, 1382 bytes).
statebundle_record_model_VERIFIED_202610.found_by: live Frida cursor-delta + nested-call probe on FUN_146af20d0/FUN_146af2340, cross-checked byte-exact against the capture, 2026-10-10

fragment_grammar_VERIFIED_20261010.what: VERIFIED fragment grammar, measured from the client's own varint reads. A fragment is `[varint KEY][varint TYPE_INDEX][self-delimiting payload]` -- the header is EXACTLY TWO varints and there is NO length field. EVIDENCE (live Frida probe hooking FUN_14087b5c0 the varint reader, FUN_146af20d0 the record reader and FUN_146af2340 the fragment reader, logging for each fragment the varints read with their offset from the fragment start): across 300 fragments the first two varints sit at offset 0 and offset 1 in EVERY SINGLE ONE, with zero exceptions; any further varints begin at offset 5 or later and are payload-internal. 48 distinct keys and 47 distinct types, and the KEY->TYPE binding is 1:1 (zero keys ever map to two types). The keys are SPARSE (0,1,2,4,5,9,10,12,13,14,16,19,20,22,27,29,31,...,77) which is what a component slot table with freed slots looks like, and the spawn record carries exactly 48 fragments with exactly 48 distinct keys -- a direct match. The payload length is NOT in the header, so it must be implied by the type: FUN_146af2340 consumes the payload through the type object's vtable +0x90, i.e. each type's reader knows its own length. CONSEQUENCE: the container is now FULLY understood down to the fragment, and what remains is the per-type payload encoding (one codec per component type) -- which is also exactly what is needed to give the player physics, since a physics component would arrive as one of these fragments. NOTE the sparse keys rule out 'key = fragment index'; key is the component's slot handle.
fragment_grammar_VERIFIED_20261010.found_by: live Frida multipoint probe (varint reader + record reader + fragment reader), 300 fragments, 2026-10-10

spawn_fragment_types_20261010.what: The 48 fragments of the spawn record (record_id 1), characterised. They carry 48 distinct keys and 47 distinct type indices, and EVERY ONE of those 47 type indices resolves to a GUID that IS present in the executable: verified 47 of 47 by scanning the image once for dashed-GUID strings (8734 found) and matching. So they are real client types, not artifacts. TRAP THAT COST TIME: typeindex.json stores GUIDs WITHOUT dashes while the executable stores them WITH dashes, so a naive `guid.encode() in exe` check returns 0 hits and wrongly suggests the types do not exist. Baseline for calibration: 3490 of the table's 7052 GUIDs appear in the image. WHAT IS STILL MISSING IS THE NAMES: these descriptors use a different layout from the component region ('<Name>�...�{GUID}') and from the message region ('<Name>��<dashed GUID>' with no braces), so the name cannot be recovered by adjacency and only 1 of the 47 currently has one. The GUIDs sit among pointer tables with no ASCII name adjacent. SIZE PROFILE (measured from consecutive cursor offsets): 13 fragments are 16 bytes or smaller, 15 are 17-64, 5 are 65-512, 10 are 513B-4KB, and 4 exceed 4KB (17176, 5913, 4843, 4754). 28 of 48 are 64 bytes or less, which is the tractable end for codec work. CONSEQUENCE: identifying which fragment carries position and which carries physics cannot be done by scanning for names; it needs the empirical route (perturb one fragment, observe the client), which is only possible now that a bundle can be rebuilt without breaking the client's parse.
spawn_fragment_types_20261010.found_by: image-wide dashed-GUID scan + per-fragment size measurement from the live cursor probe, 2026-10-10

capture_has_no_movement_state_20261010.what: What the committed capture actually contains, decoded in full (79 server->client type-0x08 bundles), because the shape decides what can and cannot be mined from it. MEASURED: 24 of the 79 bundles are 46407 bytes and all carry replication_seq 1, i.e. the SAME spawn record re-sent 24 times, byte-identical. The other 54 bundles are each DISTINCT (replication_seq 2..53, one each), sizes 78-7167 bytes, and their payloads differ from one another (checked: 0 of 21 small bundles share a payload). So the capture is one spawn record repeated plus a series of one-off records, and it is a SHORT LOGIN SESSION. This is consistent with the live measurements: the channel-1 local-player stream is byte-identical across 3038 records, and the client emits no movement message in either direction. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. It does NOT show that no captured record carries position, because the 47 types in the spawn record are still unidentified, so we cannot rule any of them out. It DOES mean there is no ongoing per-entity state stream to mine: nothing in the capture is an authoritative, updating position for any actor. The practical consequence is that a physics or position fragment cannot be obtained by replaying the capture, and that the per-type payload codecs are the crux rather than an implementation detail.
capture_has_no_movement_state_20261010.found_by: decode of all 79 capture bundles, payload/size/seq comparison, 2026-10-10

post_replay_predicate_regression_2026101.what: REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED (server-side, not client RE). PeerSession._post_replay_started() in services/world/src/azoth_world/rep.py returned self.greetings_after_replay, which is NOT 'the post-V3 flight went out': that flag is set only when the REPLAY QUEUE DRAINS. The gate-8f concurrency fix (heartbeat / input-response / activity-stream must not wait for the drain) was therefore a silent no-op and the activity-clock failure returned. EVIDENCE, live run 2026-10-10: server log shows replay-chunk 19:30:40Z..19:31:09Z (29 s), replay-complete-quiet at 19:31:09Z, and the FIRST heartbeat also at 19:31:09Z -- not one ping for the whole replay window -- while the client's OnLocalNetworkConnectionWarning burst 1 -> 104 between 19:30:44Z and 19:31:07Z, i.e. inside that window. The replay is 1278 chunks carrying 137 messages (~1090 Carrier chunks) and needs ~22-30 s at AZOTH_CHUNK_GAP_MS=20, while the client's state watchdog tears the transport down at ~27 s without an expected message. FIX: the predicate now returns self.v3_responded (the V3 registration was answered, so the flight is out and the watchdog is armed). greetings_after_replay keeps its real meaning and is still required by maybe_state_stream, which MUST wait for the drain because re-applying captured bundles is not idempotent client-side. AFTER THE FIX, measured: 20 heartbeat events fired BEFORE replay-complete-quiet (was 0); transportError 0, disconnected from REP 0, State(InGame) is timeout 0, world renders. LIMITATION, measured and NOT yet closed: the warning burst is reduced but NOT eliminated -- warnings still climb during the replay window even with heartbeat + input-response + keepalive flowing, so those are not what the activity clock counts. Per ingame_activity_timer the clock is refreshed by a message the dispatcher does NOT recognize (its MISS path), and the documented candidate is the type-0x1b88 activity stream, which is OFF by default (ACTIVITY_STREAM_ENABLED false). TEST TRAP FIXED: TestActivityClockSurvivesTheReplay._session() used to pre-set greetings_after_replay = True WHILE setting replay_queue = ['still delivering the replay'], a state production never produces mid-replay, so test_heartbeat_fires_while_the_replay_is_still_draining passed against the broken implementation. A regression test that pre-sets the very flag under test proves nothing; the helper now sets it False and the test was verified to FAIL with the buggy predicate and PASS with the fix.
post_replay_predicate_regression_2026101.found_by: live private run + world.log event timeline, 2026-10-10; validated by reverting the predicate and watching the test fail

chunk_gap_decides_the_warning_burst_2026.what: THE CAUSE OF THE `OnLocalNetworkConnectionWarning` BURST, MEASURED BY A/B ON THE DOCUMENTED CONFIGURATION. It is the REPLAY DURATION, not a missing post-replay message: while the replay is still streaming the client has not yet re-stamped its activity clock, so it warns on every interval until the replay finishes. The burst therefore lasts exactly as long as the replay, and the documented recipe (`AZOTH_CHUNK_GAP_MS=20`) makes the replay ~26 s, which straddles the client's ~27 s watchdog -- hence an intermittent death at ~27 s after the spawn. THE FOUR-RUN MATRIX, same build, no Frida attached, one variable at a time (scripts/measure-run.py, `.azoth/logs/ab-runs.jsonl`): (1) A2 chunk_gap=20, activity_stream OFF -> replay 76 s (load-degraded), replay-chunk 2155, warnings 80, `transportError` 1 + `disconnected from REP` 1 at 27 s after the spawn, WITH 32 heartbeats already sent before the drain. (2) B2 chunk_gap=20, activity_stream ON -> replay 29 s, warnings 82, 33 activity-stream messages before the drain, no transportError. (3) C-gap8 chunk_gap=8 -> replay 15 s, warnings **0**, transportError 0. (4) D-default (no AZOTH_CHUNK_GAP_MS, i.e. the code default 4 ms) -> replay 10 s, warnings **0**, transportError 0. CONCLUSIONS: (a) the type-0x1b88 activity stream does NOT reduce the warnings -- 80 vs 82 at the same gap -- so the 0x1b88-refreshes-the-clock hypothesis is REFUTED; it is not the value of the documented knob either, since the code default is 4 ms (`REPLAY_CHUNK_GAP_MS = os.environ.get("AZOTH_CHUNK_GAP_MS", "4")`) while the RUNBOOK tells operators to set 20. The burst climbs exactly while the replay stream is in flight (A2: replay 20:26:04-20:27:20, warnings 20:26:09-20:26:34) and stops when it drains. A measurement that only counts a session's total warnings therefore conflates two very different runs: 80 warnings over a 76 s replay vs 0 over a 10 s replay. (d) The chunk gap is a RISK/THROUGHPUT TRADE: at 4-8 ms the warning burst is gone but the client may exit on its own ~3 min in (D logged `Cleanup() 1`); at 20 ms the session is calmer but the replay is long enough to risk the 27 s kill. THE HONEST UNKNOWN is what makes a fast replay unstable, and that is the next measurement.

movement_message_codecs_decoded_20261011.what: The WIRE LAYOUT of the client's named movement message family, decoded statically from each type's own object-vtable marshal and unmarshal (which agree), plus the envelope. Method: each type's descriptor is built by a getter that calls FUN_1407de270(&out16, guid16, &name) then stores a codec facet at descriptor+0x48; the facet is a 6-slot table whose slot +0x20 is MARSHAL (what the client sends) and +0x28 is UNMARSHAL (what it accepts). Reading both independently is the cross-check. WIRE TYPES (index into private-client/runtime/typeindex.json) and prefix-varint bytes: MoveActorMsg 710 (86 0b, body 16 bytes = one opaque 16-byte blob and nothing else); MoveActorToHubMsg 718 and StartMovementCommunicationMsg 726 (8e 0b / 96 0b, 20 bytes = 16-byte blob + u32 BE); ProcessDeferredMovementRequestsMsg 723 and MoveAnActorMsg 84 marshal to ZERO bytes (no payload is possible); MovementTimeoutMsg 736 and CancelMovementMsg 5342 (76 bytes); AckMovementMsg 739 (113 bytes); CommitMovementMsg 740 and AbortMovementMsg 745 (40 bytes = 16 + u32 + u32 + u64 + u64); CheckMovementStatusMsg 747 has a known 76-byte layout but its reader FUN_146a59b30 reads only 16 bytes then UNCONDITIONALLY FAILS, so a server-sent CheckMovementStatusMsg can never be accepted -- do not use it; ReceivePlayerPositionClientMsg 4216 (b8 41) = 36 bytes = u64 BE + u64 BE + u64 BE + u32 BE + u32 BE + u32 BE; ReceivePlayerPositionWithCameraClientMsg 4217 (b9 41) = 48 bytes = the same 36 plus a second u32x3 group. ALL integers are BIG-endian (htonl FUN_140876cd0 / bswap64 FUN_1408770e0). For ReceivePlayerPositionClientMsg the reader FUN_143f97d10 hands the 16-byte compound at obj+0x30 to a transform-like setter, which is why the three trailing u32s are the best POSITION candidate -- order/size/type observed, SCALE and AXIS MEANING guessed. NEGATIVE RESULT kept: mapping class vtables to messages by address adjacency is WRONG; only the getter->facet edge is authoritative (messages share marshals, e.g. CommitMovementMsg and AbortMovementMsg share FUN_146a587a0).

clean_exit_at_20_minutes_20261011.what: MEASURED PATTERN: a live private session ENDS BY ITSELF at almost exactly 20 minutes after the player spawns, cleanly and without any transport error. So this is an ORDERLY logout, not a connection failure, and it is deterministic rather than load-dependent. STATIC: the string `CGame exiting to main menu` (VA 0x147fc8e98) is referenced from 0x146444b39 inside FUN_146444b10, whose exit is selected by the cvar `UIFeatures.g_exitToMainMenu` (0x147fc8c70); its sibling string is `CGame exiting to desktop, instead of main menu` (0x147fc8ed8). FUN_146444b10 has NO direct callers, so the decision arrives through a delegate/virtual dispatch. A live hook on FUN_146444b10 did NOT fire on any of the observed exits, so this function is NOT the one that runs in this scenario -- a useful negative result that redirects the search. client_record_crc32_container.what: EVERY non-chunked client->server Carrier DATA record on channels 0 and 1 is `[u32 BE crc32(payload)][u32 BE len(payload)][payload]`, and the payload is a typed Javelin message `[16-byte target id][00 01][prefix-varint wire type][body]`. Verified over one live session: 285/294 channel-0 records and 40279/40279 channel-1 records satisfy BOTH the CRC and the length field. The 9 channel-0 exceptions are the 1115 B / 239 B entries, which are MF_CHUNKS transfers carrying a different header. Independently checked on hand-picked records: ch0 36 B -> crc32 of the 28-byte payload is 0x2b0bc565 = bytes 2b 0b c5 65 and len 0x0000001c = 28; ch1 119 B -> crc32 0x3f331f2d with len 0x0000006f = 111. The server does NOT use this container: its own records are `[vlq32 len][00 01][type][body]` (the form the capture's server->client replay uses), and the client accepts that form for channel 0 (it resolves and echoes 0x15d).

ingame_activity_watchdog.what: `FUN_146445e10(conn+0x1530, expected, mode)` is the InGame activity watchdog, and it is the source of `State(InGame) is timeout : frames 10, currentTimeoutIntervalCount %d`. Decompiled: it looks up a per-type receive state (FUN_14643a610) and, when `*(int*)(state+0x10) <= conn[0x1548]`, increments a consecutive-count at `conn+0x154c`; once that count exceeds 9 it logs the line above, resets BOTH counters to 0 and returns 1. Return 1 is consumed by `FUN_14643e4a0`, which sends a disconnect notice through `FUN_146460240(conn, <reason>, ...)` where the reason is picked by the connection state (0x2f for states 1-6/9, 0x37 for 10, 0x31/0x32/0x34/0x35 for 11-14). The return byte is `b0 01` at 0x146445efb (the launcher's watchdog patch flips it to `b0 00`), and the sibling `return 0` path is `32 c0` at 0x146445f0c - so the patch is on the right instruction. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: with the patch applied the line still prints every 30 s (the log call sits before the return) but the disconnect notice is never sent, and the session still left the world at exactly 20:00 - so this watchdog is NOT the 20-minute exit.
ingame_activity_watchdog.found_by: corpus decompile + disassembly of the live build, 2026-10-11

exit_patch_0x141004230_refuted_20261011.what: ITEM 3, MEASURED AND REFUTED 2026-10-11. The claim that the 20-minute exit is one 5-byte `call CGame::ActorContainerDisconnect` at 0x141004230 is WRONG for the observed exit path. The patch was applied and byte-verified live (reverse/probes/client/frida-patch-exit-verify.py: e8dbc34105 -> 9090909090, ok:True, range r-x). The session reached InGame at 12:46:39.761 and died at 13:06:40.190 = EXACTLY 20 min 0.4 s later, with a clean `CGame exiting to main menu` + `ClientContext Cleanup()`, transportError 0 and ActorContainerDisconnect 0. After the exit the five bytes were STILL 9090909090. So the 20-minute timer is real and fires to the tenth of a second, but it does not go through 0x141004230. Also new: the previous session's death at ~18.7 min was NOT the timer -- it was a server IndexError on a compressed datagram (see the frame.py/rep.py fix), now fixed, which is why the timer became visible at all. RESOLVED 2026-10-11 by a static pass (.azoth/night/subagent-20min-exit-real-path.md): 0x141004230 is ONE STATEMENT INSIDE the teardown delegate FUN_141004100, not the teardown. The recommended patch is therefore 0x14100425F FF90D8010000 -> 909090909090, implemented as services/launcher/runtime-tools/patch-exit-to-menu.py and wired into private-run.py's PATCHES.

alc_door_and_cvars_static_20261011.what: STATIC RESOLUTION OF THE ALC DOOR (full report .azoth/night/subagent-alc-door.md). (1) The receiver of &classB->0xAA8 IS resolvable: it is the latency-metric-suppression component (sub-object at O+0x18, vtable 0x14833c1f8, slot +0x40 = FUN_1443bb670). That function STORES the pointer into a vector of 0x60-byte records; the per-frame consumer FUN_1443bc950 then READS *(&classB->0xAA8) and WRITES classB+0x1d71 / classB+0x1d78 -- it never writes a clock into +0xAA8. So the HUD stamp has no writer anywhere in .text. (2) Whole-image scan: no instruction writes an 8-byte value covering classB+0xAA8; the only +0xAA8 16-byte store on a class-A object is FUN_1449309b0; the only address-taken &classB->0xAA8 is 0x14485d425 inside FUN_14485cf30. retracted_movement_claim_20261011.what: RETRACTED: `player_moves_reliable_position_reply_20261011` claimed 'the player walks' on the strength of a screenshot diff (motion ratio 0.94x vs a 0.13-0.15x control). The claim does NOT hold, and the user reported the opposite (still cannot move). WHY IT WAS WRONG: scripts/bmp-diff.py computes `motion ratio = (mad at shift 0,0) / (best mad over +/-24 px)`. A real camera TRANSLATION makes the best shift match much better than no shift, i.e. ratio >> 1. The W-hold pair had zero-shift mad 37.21 and best mad 39.46 -- the best shift was WORSE than no shift, so ratio 0.94 means the scene changed but did NOT translate coherently. The 0.94 figure was therefore ambiguous, and the '~0.12x = no movement' convention does not apply across two different frame pairs. rmi_dispatch_facet_target_registry_20261.what: STATIC 2026-10-11, first-hand (Steam exe 8654f01d..., image base 0x140000000). The Game.log line `RMIDispatch: The facet target ID couldn't be found when trying to dispatch the RMI message.` is produced by FUN_1416bcba0: the message text is at 0x148041db0 and the channel string `RMIDispatch` at 0x148041e00, and a rip-relative xref scan finds exactly one reference to each (0x1416bccf2 and 0x1416bcc21), both inside that function. Its lookup: the key is `*(u64*)(message + 8)` (the RMI target local id from the wire, passed as `param_1 + 1`); the map is at `registry + 0x148`; `FUN_1417da460(map, &slot, key)` is an open-addressing find that hashes the 8 key bytes with FNV-1a (basis 0xcbf29ce484222325, prime 0x100000001b3), with the capacity-1 mask at map+0x40, the empty-slot sentinel at map+0x50, and entries at map+0x68 with stride 0x10. On a hit the dispatcher returns `*(u64*)(*(u64*)(registry + 0x1b0) + index*0x10 + 8)` (slot-vector base +0x1b0, size index +0x188); on a miss it logs and returns 0. FUN_1416bcb20 is the sibling getter with the empty-map short-circuit. FUN_143f97bf0 is slot +0x58 of the 4216 object vtable 0x1482ea3e8 and is the caller on the position path: it dispatches through FUN_1416bcba0, then QueryInterfaces the returned target for the GUID from FUN_143fb2b90 and, if bound, calls its vtable +0x40 with the three floats read from the message at +0x30. First-hand verification of that shape: the vtable 0x1482ea3e8 reads +0x30=0x143f97f40 (type-GUID getter), +0x58=0x143f97bf0 (delivery), +0x60=0x143f97c70 (marshal), +0x68=0x143f97d10 (reader), and FUN_143fb2b90 parses the literal interface string `{17C00FC6-074F-47EB-9640-9743D890ED6F}` at 0x1482ea938. So the observed error means the client has no RMI target registered under the local id the server sent (0x1A954ABC4B3185BF). Whether that id is wrong or the target was never created is exactly what the registry dump must answer; do not change the 4216 body before it.

wire_type_names_from_binary_20261012.what: METHOD + RESULTS, 2026-10-12, first-hand. Every Javelin type's NAME can be recovered from the binary without Ghidra: `private-client/runtime/typeindex.json` lists `typeIndex[wire index] = GUID`, and for each of those GUIDs the client's `.rdata` holds the GUID **as a dashed lowercase string** immediately preceded by a NUL-terminated AZ RTTI name. Search the exe for the dashed GUID, skip back over the NUL, and read the preceding run of printable bytes. CORRECTIONS this produced (they change how three levers should be read):: (1) **wire 1589 (`0x635`) is `ActionListComponentServerFacet_ReceiveInputFromClient`** - the client's channel-1 stream is NOT an unnamed 'local player state stream', it is an RMI call on the server-side ActionList component facet; (2) **wire 4246 (`0x1096`) is `TimeComponentClientFacet_SyncTimeChange` and 4247 (`0x1097`) is `TimeComponentClientFacet_SyncDayPhase`** - the lever the atlas calls `AZOTH_REPLAY_INPUT_RESPONSE` replays TIME SYNC messages, not input responses, which also identifies the recurring `2 x SyncTimeChange + 2 x SyncDayPhase` facet-target errors; (3) wire 349 (`0x15d`) resolves to the string `{85C7E01E-55DE-4A6E-AFC5-80FA9A8AD260}` - CORRECTED later the same day: 349 is **`PingMsg`**; further printable runs precede that GUID, so when a GUID is preceded by NUL padding the reader must take the LONGEST adjacent printable run, not the first. Caveat: types whose GUID is absent as a dashed string (e.g. 669/0x29d, 5397/0x1515) are not Javelin-typed in this sense - they belong to another registry - so a name lookup that returns nothing is informative, not a bug.

ipositionreceiver_vtable_layout_20261012.what: STATIC 2026-10-12, first-hand byte reads (Steam exe 8654f01d, image base 0x140000000). Two distinct vtables matter, and confusing them is the reason the QI result was hard to read. (A) The IPositionReceiver INTERFACE vtable is **0x1482eb160**: slot +0x20 = 0x143fadd00, the QueryInterface that returns `this` when the queried GUID equals IPositionReceiver's. (B) The family's BASE/type vtable is **0x1482ea4e8**, and its layout is: +0x00 = 0x143f983f0 (scalar deleting destructor: writes the vtable then frees 0x10 bytes when the low bit of the flag is set), +0x08 = 0x1407c7df0 (zero two qwords), +0x10 = 0x143f98300 (REGISTER BY NAME: leas the string `IPositionReceiver` at 0x1482ea920 and passes it to a registry call at `[rax+8]` on global+0x30), +0x18 = 0x141177250, **+0x20 = 0x140294860 = `c2 00 00` = `ret 0`** (returns null), +0x28 = 0x143f983d0 (the INTERFACE-VTABLE INSTALLER: `lea rax,[rip+0x4352d84]` -> 0x1482eb160, `mov [r8],rax`, `mov byte [rdx+1],1`, i.e. it stamps the interface vtable onto a sub-object), +0x30 = 0x140294970, +0x38 = 0x143f98430, +0x40 = 0x143f98450, +0x48 = 0x1402948d0, +0x50 = 0x1402948b0, +0x58 = 0x143f98470, +0x60 = 0x143f98480, +0x68 = 0x140294910 (`xor al,al; ret`), +0x70 = 0x143f98490, +0x78 = 0x143f98610. For a base-typed object that slot is `ret 0`, so the QI returns null; only an object whose vtable is an interface vtable like 0x1482eb160 can answer. This is exactly the measured live result: 37063 registered targets, 225 distinct vtables, 0 that answer IPositionReceiver. Note also 0x143f983d0 is reached as slot +0x28 of the base vtable, which is how the interface sub-object acquires 0x1482eb160.

az_interface_decoupler_mechanism_2026101.what: STATIC 2026-10-12, first-hand. The message-to-interface routing is AZ's interface-decoupler mechanism, and the mangled template names survive in .rdata, which names every piece: `RegisterInterfaceDecoupler<IPositionReceiver>(const IPositionReceiver*, AZStd::vector<AZStd::function<void(ReflectContext*)>>&)`, `InstallRegistrationHook<VReceivePlayerPositionClientMsg, IPositionReceiver, Hub, Amazon>`, `InstallRegistrationHook<VReceivePlayerPositionWithCameraClientMsg, IPositionReceiver>`, and the equivalents for ISpectabilityListener, ISpectatedVitalsListener and SpectatedPlayerComponent. So `StartMovementCommunicationMsg` was the wrong lever from the start, which is consistent with the measured result that sending it reliably on channel 0 changed nothing (`start_movement_reliable_ch0_does_not_bind_receiver_20261012`). The real local-player position plumbing is a DIFFERENT family, named in the same string table: `PlayerPositionTrackingComponent` (GUID 62620B33-6F37-418B-9C4F-62AD6058D54D) with `PlayerPositionTrackingComponentClientFacet` (B74D06BC-123E-4C39-A842-EB8CDE4B6DAF) and `PlayerPositionTrackingComponentServerFacet` (7A014FFD-A6FD-418F-ABF0-2EBD64B6785D), `PositionInTheWorldComponent`, `PositionalTicketingComponent`, `CameraPositionListener`, and `IPositionReceiver` itself. client_facet_creation_is_a_by_name_facto.what: STATIC, first-hand, second session of 2026-10-12. This answers 'what makes the client create a client-side facet for a component'. Every client facet is constructed by a PER-CLASS BY-NAME FACTORY, of the shape: `lVar = ReflectionRegistry.CreateByName("<Class>", <size>, <align>, ...); <owner> + 0x80 = <ctor>(lVar); <facet> + 8 = <owner>;`. The registry is the global at 0x14a313ff8 - the SAME object that backs the `IPositionReceiver` register-by-name (FUN_143f98300) and installer (FUN_143f983d0), so 'create the ClientFacet' and 'create the IPositionReceiver instance' are the same question about the same registry. FACTORY TABLE SIGNATURE (reproducible, no Ghidra): each class owns a table whose tail is `[0x1406c7b30][0x1416a1340][FACTORY][0x14171a8b0][0x1417aae90]`. Scanning for that tail finds 369 tables with 368 distinct names, and 368/368 of them are `*ComponentClientFacet` - the family is exactly the client facets. Tool `reverse/tools/scan-client-facets.py --check`; output `research/derived/client-facet-factories.json`. THE FACTORY IS NEVER CALLED DIRECTLY: `callers.py` reports 0 callers for 0x142cff160, 0x145c209f0 and 0x142605970, and 0x142cff160's address exists in the image only as the 8-byte pointer at its table slot 0x148139660. So facet creation is table-driven, and the open question is which engine path walks those tables. FAMILY CREATORS: a second, larger function creates the whole facet family for a component and is likewise never called directly - 0x142d14d50 creates the PlayerPositionTracking family in sequence (0x142cdea80, 0x142cdece0 = the ClientFacet, 0x142cdef40) and 0x145c94990 does the same for the PositionInTheWorld family (0x145b18c90, 0x145b18ef0, 0x145b19150, plus PersistentPositionInTheWorldData). Both take the entity from FUN_1404b67b0 and are reached only through tables (0x142d14d50 has NO 8-byte pointer site at all). NEGATIVE RESULTS THAT MATTER: (1) `IPositionReceiver` is NOT in the 368 - it is not a client facet, which is why no RMI target is an instance of it; (2) there is NO `CharacterPhysicsComponentClientFacet` in this build at all, independent corroboration of `physics_components_absent_RESOLVED_20261012` and of the old {B1237004-...} GUID being a different type; (3) there is no ActorMover facet, consistent with `actormover_is_hub_migration_not_locomotion_20261012`. WHY THIS IS DECISIVE FOR THE MOVEMENT WORK: the class the entity is missing is NOT missing from the build. On the live entity 22 of 26 named components have a matching `*ComponentClientFacet` class registered (PlayerPositionTrackingComponent, CharacterComponent, TraversalComponent, CameraLockComponent, PlayerInputFiltersComponent, PlayerAOIComponent, InterestComponent, SpectatorModeComponent, SpectatedPlayerComponent, PlayerTimeComponent, PlayerDataBroadcastComponent, HUDComponent, DebugRenderComponent, AsyncRenderTransformComponent, NavMeshConstraintComponent, DetectableObjectComponent, AttributeComponent, CombatStatusComponent, UnstuckComponent, ActivateVirtualInputComponent, PlayerAppearanceComponent, and Transform via Game/AsyncRenderTransform). So 'the class does not exist' is excluded. NEXT MEASUREMENT (cheap, one number per component): the facet slot is `component + 0x80`. For each of the 126 components of the live local-player entity, read `[component+0x80]`. If it is null for ALL of them, the local player entity receives NO client facets at all and the problem is general; if it is non-null for most and null only for the position family, the problem is specific and the family creator 0x142d14d50 is the thing to hook. The existing probe `reverse/probes/client/frida-player-components-full.py` already walks the list and resolves each component's vtable slot 0, so it needs only the extra read.
